name: Camp stove (propane, white-gas, multi-fuel and butane)

fuels: unleaded petrol (Dual Fuel and multi-fuel models)
combustion.note: All exhaust goes into the room; makers say outdoor use only. Some butane tabletop stoves are made for indoor restaurant tables (CPSC), still with ventilation and never for heat. The kW figure is from two single-burner stoves; others differ.

comps.spec: 1 lb (16.4 oz) disposable propane cylinders, often part-full spares stored with the stove; butane cassette cans (227 g) for tabletop stoves. Never refill a disposable cylinder, and never puncture or burn a used one
comps.loc: Screwed into the regulator, or in the stove case or gear bin

comps.spec: White gas (Coleman fuel, naphtha) in the tank or a spare can; Dual Fuel models also run on unleaded petrol, multi-fuel stoves on kerosene. Never kerosene or leaded fuel in a Coleman stove
comps.loc: Stove tank or fuel bottle, and cans on the shelf nearby

comps.spec: Preset propane regulator (10 psi on one Coleman propane stove) that the cylinder screws into; makers say don't adjust it. Keep it with its own stove
comps.loc: Side of the stove, between cylinder and burner

comps.spec: Burner control valves turned by the knobs, one per burner, plus a lighting lever on Coleman white-gas stoves
Generator tube on white-gas stoves: carries fuel from the tank valve into the mixing chamber above the burner. A wear part, sold as a spare; don't bend it
comps.loc: From the tank valve into the burner box

comps.spec: Hand air pump in the fuel tank or bottle: plunger, pump cup and one-way check valve. About 30 strokes pressurises a Coleman tank. Keep the cup oiled
comps.loc: Front of the fuel tank, or the top of an MSR fuel bottle

comps.spec: Detachable fuel tank on Coleman white-gas stoves, or a separate fuel bottle with a pump on MSR-type stoves; holds fuel under pump pressure. Fill outdoors with the tank off the stove
comps.loc: Clipped to the front or end of the stove

comps.spec: Piezo spark igniter on butane cassette and Jetboil-type stoves, and a rotary ignitor knob on electronic-ignition Coleman Dual Fuel models. Some stoves have none and are lit with a match
comps.loc: Beside the control knob; electrode at the burner

comps.spec: Cooking grate, case and fold-out wind baffles; a cassette stove's grate must sit right way up
comps.loc: Top and sides of the stove

comps.spec: O-rings and pump seals in the pump, fuel line and canister socket; they stiffen and leak below freezing
comps.loc: Pump, fuel line joints and canister socket

buildings.loc: Store, office and left at sites
Butane tabletop stoves for buffets and table cooking

notes: Built for outdoors: propane, white-gas and multi-fuel camp stoves make carbon monoxide and their makers forbid using them in a house, camper or tent, or for heat. Butane cassette stoves are a separate tabletop design whose canister bay can explode if a big pan, a griddle or a second stove heats it. Take the cylinder off, or depressurise the fuel bottle, before storing (Coleman propane stove, MSR WhisperLite), keep spare fuel outside the living space, and never puncture or burn a used can or cylinder (EMSD hot pot).
